Comments (English): [ Great for a family of 3 ] || ---------------- || 1. Reason for purchase I bought a 12-person third-party dishwasher in 2018 and used it well, but I had to buy a new one because I moved. It's so convenient that I use more than one dishwasher a day, but I'm moving to a two-year-old rental, so I was reluctant to buy a built-in one, so I was considering a 12-person and a 6-person one, and bought a 6-person one. I didn't buy it myself, so I had to choose between a 6-person one that doesn't have any perforations and doesn't require cutting the mop holder, but there weren't as many products as I thought, so I chose a Samsung product that I could trust for after-sales service. 2. Product pros and cons 1) Spacious interior I'm used to a 12-person one. I thought it might be too small because it's a 6-person one, but I like that the interior is wider than I thought. Of course, it holds less than the 12-person one with the upper and lower sections, but it's deep, so I can wash more than I thought. I think it's not half the size of a 12-person one, but about 60%. I live in a family of three, so it can hold not only simple morning dishes, but also dinner, and pots or frying pans that are too deep or big, or dishes for 3 people, side dishes, and cooking utensils. 2) Perforation If you rent or rent out, it would be difficult if you need to cut the mop holder for a 12-person built-in, but this product doesn't require that, so it's easy to install. A technician will come and install it, but it seems like it would be easy to just remove it and move without a technician. I gave up on the 12-person one when I moved and left it behind because the removal and reinstallation cost was in the mid-to-late 100,000 won range, so I bought it with the intention of spending a little more and buying a new one, and I think I made a good decision. Sometimes, those who don't have a sink hole may need a hole, so check before purchasing. These days, apartment sinks have holes for detergent holes, but some don't, so it's essential to check before installation. 3) Automatic door opening This is a function that anyone who has used a dishwasher would think is absolutely necessary. In order for the dishes to dry after washing, unless they are completely dried by hot air, you have to open them one by one if they don't open. 4) I don't feel any major disadvantages and I'm using it well. 3. Overall review It's a suitable size that can be installed without drilling due to the structure or because it's not my own. Those who are looking for a dishwasher should I recommend the Samsung dishwasher over the Jeolmi. It seems to be cost-effective, considering that it is easy to get after-sales service in case of defects, breakdowns, or moving. It is suitable for a household of 2-3 people or for people who do not cook every day.

My wife and I looked at Miele, Bosch, and other higher end dishwashers. But nothing beat the flexibility and innovative layout of the three racks in this KitchenAid dishwasher. We've been using it for a month now and are very happy with it. Key advantages:. 1. The top rack is really useful. It provides a spot for 10 dirty cups/glasses. That frees up space for other items in the main rack. The top rack also has an area for large, flat utensil like kitchen knives, spatulas, etc. Perfect. 2. The main and bottom racks have plenty of room for the remaining dirty dishes. We prefer the removable cutlery holder over competing dishwashers that use the top rack, non-removable rack for cutlery. Plus the Miele and Bosch racks are smaller. Overall, we're finding that this dishwasher can hold way more dishes than our old dishwasher. 3. Super quiet. 4. We actually find the lights in the interior to be very useful! I'm happy we paid a little more for this feature. It's easier to place and retrieve specific items with the well-lit interior. 5. I prefer the traditional North American drying system over the "more efficient" but less effective European drying systems of the Miele and Bosch. Dishes come out completely dry. 6. Importantly, our dishes are all coming out clean. 7. My wife loves the indicator LED on the front. Blue for cleaning. Red for drying. White for done. Plus there is a countdown digital timer on the top edge of the door. 8. We added an extended warranty for a total of 5 years of coverage.

Sentence (English): I own an appliance repair company and have worked on more dishwashers than I can count.
Comments (English): [ An appliance technician's opinion.  ] || ---------------- || I own an appliance repair company and have worked on more dishwashers than I can count. I estimate over 1000+ dishwashers.I was in the market for a new dishwasher, since our used Whirlpool was no longer cutting it. (would not spray hard enough, would Never dry. Ever) I always thought Bosch dishwashers were out of my reach, price wise. However, having caught this Bosch dishwasher 100 series on sale at $599 (plus a $50 cash back from retail me not, which I have not seen yet) I couldn't resist and had to give it a shot.I was so glad I did! It's nothing super fancy. My model lacks the upper 3rd rack, which I thibk would be a great feature.However, this dishwsher simply works! It's imperceptibly quiet, looks beautiful, feels more solid than any other dishwasher on the market (in this price point) and above all. Actually. Cleans. The. Dishes. I was very skeptical about the drying ability of the dishwasher as it used what's called condensation drying. It jets the dishes during the final rinse to a very high temp, the stainless exterior tub cools faster than the dishes do, and thus the moisture is attracted to the outer tub, where it drops down and drains away.All of this sounds made up and had me convinced it would not work at all. Comments (English): [ My 20 year old Bosch 800 was designed way better ] || ---------------- || This was replacing our 20 year old Bosch 800 series that finally died. This newer version is just not as good. The slots in the lower rack are way too tight. It's hard to fit our dinner plates to fit between the tines. They're heavily slanted but the sides the glasses rest on are vertical. Not a lot of clearance. If you put the middle rack down so you can fit tall glasses, the plates on the lower rack hit the washer arm. If you put the middle rack in the upper position, the glasses hit the upper rack. The wash cycle is very long, over 2.5 hours! The crystaldry feature is great, but if you don't empty the dishwashe right after, water starts condensing inside. It catches halfway out to the point you have to yank on it. I wish the handle matched the door. The handle looks to be alumunim, not stainless like the door. The controls are very annoying. If you want to change the type of cycle you want to run after you picked one, you have to go through a long reset process. Even if you didn't already start the cycle. Our old one, you could switch easily and even clear it without a long reset process. It is very quiet. I've always been a proponent of Bosch dishwashers so I was quite disappointed by this one.

Sentence (English): We moved to a different home last year from a house we had lived in for 29 years.
Comments (English): [ Nothing But A Bosch ] || ---------------- || We moved to a different home last year from a house we had lived in for 29 years. My wife and I are both retired and this was an opportunity to downsize our living space and possessions. A selling point was that the previous owners of our new home left all the major appliances, all of which were relatively new. The dishwasher (not a Bosch) was top-of-the-line and in good condition. Unfortunately for us, we were comparing it to the Bosch we had purchased for our previous house. No comparison! We were now having to rinse everything that went into the washer. Drawers in the machine would only pull 2/3 of the way out, making loading a circus act. And it seemed we were running it constantly - so much less room than our previous Bosch. So after a few months of growling and grumbling, we ordered Bosch and had the installers carry a perfectly good, almost new dishwasher away. Downsizing is not a bad thing, but our Bosch dishwasher will not be a part of our downsizing for the rest of our lives. We want nothing but a Bosch.

Comments (English): [ Bosch 300 series ] || ---------------- || Installation process was smooth due to various instructions including videos, cards on the unit, etc. quite spacious compared to our previous 100 series purchased 12 years ago. Love the rack placement & arrangements, remains the same as previous Bosch dishwashers, but added bonus of a few extra adjustable ones. Middle racks is easily adjusted up or down to acccommodate larger pots/cookware. The upper rack takes care of this small loose items typically hard to place. Appreciate the overall consistency of this product with our previous one, I.e. cleaning the filter, jet placements, rinse& soap dispensers. Our previous one lasted over 12 yrs running at least twice per day for our busy family of five, washing dirty pots, pans and crusted plates. Hoping this one will serve us as well. We've had this one for nearly one month, and we are happy overall with the purchase. Gave it a 4/5 for several reasons. The looks, got the white one, it's exterior is a little plain. Lost another point for the programming. Buttons are not straightforward if you don't want to use the app to manage the cycles. Finally, one last thing is the middle rack is a little wobbly side-to-side, which was an issue with my original one. But I see that Bosch reinforced the front wheels with a long plastic support. Had to gradually replace the 4 wheels on my previous model.

Lost another point for the programming. Buttons are not straightforward if you don't want to use the app to manage the cycles. Finally, one last thing is the middle rack is a little wobbly side-to-side, which was an issue with my original one. But I see that Bosch reinforced the front wheels with a long plastic support. Had to gradually replace the 4 wheels on my previous model.

Sentence (English): This was replacing our 20 year old Bosch 800 series that finally died.
Comments (English): [ My 20 year old Bosch 800 was designed way better ] || ---------------- || This was replacing our 20 year old Bosch 800 series that finally died. This newer version is just not as good.The slots in the lower rack are way too tight. It's hard to fit our dinner plates to fit between the tines. In general, this model has way more slots than our old one but fits less plates and glasses.The angles on the middle rack don't make sense. They're heavily slanted but the sides the glasses rest on are vertical.Not a lot of clearance. If you put the middle rack down so you can fit tall glasses, the plates on the lower rack hit the washer arm. If you put the middle rack in the upper position, the glasses hit the upper rack.The wash cycle is very long, over 2.5 hours! The crystaldry feature is great, but if you don't empty the dishwashe right after, water starts condensing inside.We do like the top rack feature but would be nice if it wasn't in the way of items in the middle rack. That's mostly due to bad design of the middle rack.The top rack doesn't pull out smoothly. It catches halfway out to the point you have to yank on it.I wish the handle matched the door. The handle looks to be alumunim, not stainless like the door.The controls are very annoying. If you want to change the type of cycle you want to run after you picked one, you have to go through a long reset process. Even if you didn't already start the cycle. Our old one, you could switch easily and even clear it without a long reset process.It is very quiet.I've always been a proponent of Bosch dishwashers so I was quite disappointed by this one.

Sentence (English): Replaced a 12 yr old dishwasher with this smansy Bosh, love the cleaning settings and its cool that the app tells you when its done and what cycle (my kid) choose.

I noticed that if I don't secure some lighter items and set to blast that area (front or back or front/back) the item might "flip" and hold water, so working that issue out. Otherwise, unit is SUPER quiet, has a red light on the floor when its on, app gives status, and it works just fantastic!

One set of tines folds down (with difficulty) and the other does not. With or without the tines folded down, the space for dishes is very narrow and would not work with pasta bowls or any plates with a slight curve. We have no idea what the Bosch designers had in mind for this. Even the cheapest dishwashers have a better arrangement. Well, yes, that could be done--but it takes extra time to align the dinnerware so these do not overlap and hit the top of the dishwasher. We think the third rack is just a sales gimmick. The basket is easier and quicker. Apart from the above, we would advise great caution in ordering any dishwasher from Lowes online. We added the fees for the dishwasher, parts, installation, etc to the shopping cart list. The total on the check-out page was higher than it should have been by several hundred dollars. Comments (English): [ leaks, but can be fixed ] || ---------------- || I like the dishwasher, WDT750SAKZ0, but there is a design flaw in the steel tub which enables a leak on the left side of the dishwasher onto the floor just in front of the left foot. I did not use the dishwasher for months after installation until I had time to troubleshoot the leak. At the point where the top and bottom parts of the tub are crimped together, that joint causes the front tub edge to bend out slightly. This is directly next to the door hinge. Because of the spin direction of the lower spray arm, water splashes through the small gap created by the flared out tub crimp on the left side only. To solve this problem I did two things. I removed the gasket/door seal W******** (now W********) that is in the tub, and reinstalled it while stretching it a little so there would be slightly more extra gasket bending into the bottom of the tub. I also cut a piece of flat rubber just thick enough to slightly straighten out the flared tub edge at the crimp and prevent the splash-through leak. I epoxied the rubber to the back of the left hinge. No more leak.

Sentence (English): I like the dishwasher, WDT750SAKZ0, but there is a design flaw in the steel tub which enables a leak on the left side of the dishwasher onto the floor just in front of the left foot.
Comments (English): [ leaks, but can be fixed ] || ---------------- || I like the dishwasher, WDT750SAKZ0, but there is a design flaw in the steel tub which enables a leak on the left side of the dishwasher onto the floor just in front of the left foot. I did not use the dishwasher for months after installation until I had time to troubleshoot the leak. At the point where the top and bottom parts of the tub are crimped together, that joint causes the front tub edge to bend out slightly. This is directly next to the door hinge. Because of the spin direction of the lower spray arm, water splashes through the small gap created by the flared out tub crimp on the left side only. To solve this problem I did two things. I removed the gasket/door seal W11035860 (now W11483553) that is in the tub, and reinstalled it while stretching it a little so there would be slightly more extra gasket bending into the bottom of the tub. Sentence (English): As backround, I had a different manufacturer's dish drawers that were in use for 17 years.
Comments (English): [ Cafe 24 Inch Wide Double Drawer Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || As backround, I had a different manufacturer's dish drawers that were in use for 17 years. I read reviews on the Cafe dish drawers and wanted a cohesive look in my remodeled kitchen. My previous experience with my old dish drawers was very good. PROS: I do like the "China" setting as I use vintage dishes on a daily basis; the units clean well; the depth in the top drawer does hold a 12" platter; racks are easily removed for a custom for for pots/pans, large bowls. CONS: The cafe dish drawers are the same dimensions for installation as my other Manufacturer's dish drawers but the interior lacks the space that I am used to. I do not use oversized glasses or dishes. I find that the racks in my Cafe appliance are not spaced well for glasses or coffee cups and any dishes with a slight flare on the the edges will nest if not carefully spaced; if the bottom rack is used for glasses/cups the upper, side rack(s) can not be used unless careful spacing is done as the water can not reach to clean. This is plenty of space for a 2 person household for every 2 day wash using just the upper drawer and hand washing pots/pans. If you wash your pans in the dishwasher all of the time expect to use both drawers. For a 4 person household expect everyday washing and most likely both drawers.Would I purchase again? Although these dish drawers function properly and are a handsome appliance, no, I would purchase the brand I had previously.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher at the height of supply chain crisis as our first Bosch product back in July '21 from Home Depot with 3 year warranty.
Comments (English): [ Dishwasher rusting bad internally after a few year ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher at the height of supply chain crisis as our first Bosch product back in July '21 from Home Depot with 3 year warranty. We wanted to purchase Kitchen Aid but didnt want to wait multiple months and the Bosch was more readily available at Home Depot. We bought it because of brand name, availability, great reviews and because of claim of spotless dishes. After we got it, we found it left our hard-plastic clear drinking glasses with spots, but didnt have the desire to return it (because of supply chain issues). Then about a year and half or so later, it started rusting on the inside. We were thinking it was outside of the original 12 month warranty so we didnt file a claim. The rust became more worse over time. We forgot that we originally purchased a 3 year warranty and reached out to Home Depot to make a warranty claim. Apparently rust is not covered. We also reached out to Bosch and they told us to contact Home Depot. We had a few back and forth between the two. In fact the Bosch customer service person said they never heard of such a thing. Well, I have pictures to prove it. Regardless, no one wants to help us and we now have a less than 3 year old high-end dishwasher that is rusting. We dont plan on keeping this. I dont think I will ever buy Bosch again. We buy many high-end brands and this will be the last Bosch - they dont stand behind their product. It's too bad.

Sentence (English): This is our second Bosch Dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher; sensitive output hose ] || ---------------- || This is our second Bosch Dishwasher. Therefore, I and the Best Buy Geek Squad guy started looking at the installation—two machines with the same code. However, there a is a port on the garbage disposal, which was how my 900 at the old house dumped its waste water. The Geek Squad guy installed the hose into the garbage disposal, and opened the side of the cupboard a bit so that the hose had more flexibility when the dishwasher was slid into position. Now we have had a Bosch washing dishes for more than 10 days with no error messages. YES!

The replacement gave us an E61-3 error. It was telling us that the dump hose was not moving the waste water out. The second replacement gave the same error. Therefore, I and the Best Buy Geek Squad guy started looking at the installation—two machines with the same code. The Geek Squad guy installed the hose into the garbage disposal, and opened the side of the cupboard a bit so that the hose had more flexibility when the dishwasher was slid into position. Now we have had a Bosch washing dishes for more than 10 days with no error messages. YES!

Sentence (English): We did not want a new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Impressive! ] || ---------------- || We did not want a new dishwasher. Our beloved Hobart KitchenAid had been our only dishwasher since we bought our house in 1992. The dishwasher was built in 1974 and it was built to last. We only repaired it twice in 30 years. But now, the dishwasher could not be repaired and needed to be replaced. We scoured Consumer Reports and read about all the top rated dishwashers. Bosch was in all the top ratings. We decided on one from the 500 series because it had the third rack for silverware, adjustable rack heights, it was quiet, it would pop open upon completion of cycle to air dry and the handle was recessed. Sentence (English): Bought this dishwasher to replace another Whirlpool dishwasher that was about 8 years old and had begun to leak.
Comments (English): [ New and improved ] || ---------------- || Bought this dishwasher to replace another Whirlpool dishwasher that was about 8 years old and had begun to leak. Whirlpool has never disappointed me and this dishwasher is no exception! The redesigned third rack is more useful than the old one! You can fit coffee cups as well as small juice glasses and fruit bowls as well as knives and tongs (the old design could only fit flat items). Plenty of room on the other two racks for dishes and pots and pans. I wasn't sure I would like the silverware caddy being on the bottom rack as it used to be in the door on my old one, but not only is it great, but you really aren't sacrificing any room by having it there! This dishwasher is very quiet and doesn't require prewash of dishes or pots and pans, simply remove loose food and let the dishwasher do its job! Even baked on food comes off! The only con is the length of time the cycle runs, which is a little over 3 hours but it's not bad if you are running it at night with a full load! This one has a leak detection system to avoid the issue we had with our old one. The location of the controls is improved, instead of being all across the top (which would sometimes cause me to inadvertently hit the buttons with my leg as I emptied it), the new controls are over in the top right corner. I have been very pleased with this dishwasher and highly recommend it!

The upside is Whirpool did an amazing job getting a technician out to our house to reseal the machine, which seems to be working. I am a little bit weary as how long my dishwasher will last now, as I wanted this to be at least a 5 year product and not a throw away, keep fixing it product.

Sentence (English): This Samsung dishwasher has been a nightmare since I've owned it.
Comments (English): [ BUYER BEWARE ] || ---------------- || This Samsung dishwasher has been a nightmare since I've owned it. After less than 6 months, the dishwasher kept tripping a breaker. When the issue arrived a 3rd time, I called geek squad again and was told that I had to go through Samsung since the item was still under factory warranty. I reluctantly call Samsung and get the run around again. Since I mentioned that the breaker is tripped when the dishwasher turns on, I was told that this was an electrical issue and had nothing to do with the dishwasher. This decision was made without sending a technician to inspect my dishwasher. I was then told that I MUST hire an electrician to diagnose my electrical system before they would agree to assign a tech to come out. I did that and the electrician charged me $250 for his services. This did not resolve the dishwasher issue. I reached out to Samsung again and was basically told “tough luck” on the $250 I wasted at their request. I'm now waiting for Samsung to come out to “fix” this dishwasher. Buyer beware! I've been a Samsung customer for a long time and this is my first bad experience. This experience is bad enough for me to never buy Samsung again!

Sentence (English): Over a 40-year period we have always used KitchenAid (or Whirlpool) appliances in two homes.
Comments (English): [ Possible installation problem in older homes. ] || ---------------- || Over a 40-year period we have always used KitchenAid (or Whirlpool) appliances in two homes. This dishwasher turned out to become a problem even before it was turned on the first time. The first problem, and a major one, was that the water inlet pipe was in a new position as compared to the previous unit(s). Our appliance store could not install it and we had to hire a plumber to reroute the water supply pipe from the basement, through the kitchen floor to the unit. Instead of paying the standard $ 99 for installation, which was refunded by our appliance store, we paid $ 375 to a licensed plumber who did a great job.The second problem is one of common sense. The silverware tray does not have a sidewall riser on the dishwasher frame side to prevent knifes and other long handle utensils from banging into the wall of the dishwasher. A KitchenAid dishwasher installed in our vacation home in February 2018 has a silverware tray that has a side wall high enough to prevent long handled utensils from banging in the frame, in addition to slotted and positionable silverware covers.One savings grace is that the third rack is well designed and adds great convenience for storing glassware and ladles allowing for the lower two racks to handle many more dishes of various diameters and styles.

Because of our satisfaction with our old one we decided to get another one. Imagine our disappointment when we used it the first time and discovered wet dishes because it has no dry cycle or vent. After reading the trouble shooting tips, we discovered that we must be with it when it completes the wash cycle and open the door to vent the steam out so dishes will air dry! Not having a dry cycle would is one thing, but at least have a vent so we don't have to babysit with it or dry dishes! Would not have bought it if we had known this.
